content:
Ramón Ayala Jr., son of Norteño music icon Ramón Ayala Sr., turned himself in to the Hidalgo Police Department on Friday, October 23, and was charged with sexual assault, a second-degree felony, according to Hidalgo County jail records and attorneys involved in the case.

An arrest warrant was obtained the day before Ayala Jr. surrendered, according to a statement from the Buzbee Law Firm. He was booked into jail and arraigned, then released the same day after posting a $2,000 bond, jail records show. An emergency protective order was also obtained for the alleged victim.

The criminal charge comes after a series of civil lawsuits filed since February by former employees and touring personnel associated with Ramón Ayala y Sus Bravos del Norte, alleging repeated sexual assault, harassment, and other misconduct. Houston attorney Tony Buzbee represents the people who filed those lawsuits. The criminal case is separate from the civil lawsuits.

Attorneys for the Ayala family have denied the allegations. Ramón Ayala Sr.'s attorney, Ray Thomas, said in a statement that allegations are not evidence and an accusation is not a conviction. Ayala Jr.'s attorney did not immediately comment, according to ValleyCentral.

Ayala Jr. is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law. The charge against him is an allegation.

Sources: San Antonio Express-News, Facebook, October 25, 2026; Tejano Nation, October 24, 2026; ValleyCentral / Nexstar KVEO; Hidalgo County jail records as reported.
